title: An AI Breakthrough Has Made Decades of Computer Science Research ‘Irrelevant’ | WIRED
body: As for Linköping’s Jonsson, he plans to revisit both his own and others’ papers that hinge on ETH being true, and believes his conference paper may eventually be salvageable through another method. [...] Researchers have also been overwhelmed by the volume of content now being produced, thanks to AI, including slop-level results. Midway through the interview, Husfeldt receives what he suspects to be an AI-generated 17-page paper on the consequences of the ETH result from a random Gmail account. He won’t read it: “Reading math is a very big investment of cognitive time,” he says. title: India's New CEA Cybersecurity Regulations: What Power Sector Leaders Need to Know Before April 2027
body:
Cybersecurity has become a strategic imperative for critical infrastructure operators worldwide, and India's power sector is no exception. With the publication of the Central Electricity Authority (Cyber Security in Power Sector) Regulations, 2026, the Indian government has introduced one of the most comprehensive cybersecurity compliance frameworks ever applied to the country's electricity ecosystem. The regulations come into force on 1 April 2027 and apply to generation, transmission, [...] ## A New Era of Cybersecurity Compliance for India's Power Sector

The CEA Cyber Security Regulations represent a significant evolution in India's approach to protecting critical energy infrastructure. Rather than focusing narrowly on compliance, the regulations encourage organisations to build long-term cyber resilience across both IT and OT environments. [...] A recurring theme throughout the regulations is visibility.

Entities are required to maintain detailed cyber asset registers, classify critical systems, document network architectures, identify communication protocols and continuously assess cyber risks associated with those assets. Organisations must also maintain risk assessment and mitigation plans and periodically update them.

title: The anatomy of technology regulation | Brookings
body: While Australia is charting its own course on everything from encryption laws and extremist content to power imbalances between digital platforms and older news media organizations, New Zealand is building international partnerships on many of the same issues, such as through the Christchurch Call initiative. Meanwhile, Canada is doing more listening than acting, with its most recent attempt to pass online legislation ensuring that internet-era streaming companies face the same regulations as [...] Policy decisions thus can be motivated either by a desire to bolster domestic activity (to help a country’s producers or workers) or by a desire to promote activity internationally (to support domestic exporters). Given that technology policies tend to require compliance systems or create liability regimes that deter business creation or foreign investment, economic impact also must be factored into decisionmakers’ calculus. [...] The resulting policy fragmentation is often attributed to differing values and political ideologies within key jurisdictions: the United States, the European Union, and China. In this narrative, the U.S. prefers digital laissez-faire; Europe opts for digital big-state socialism; and China pursues a politically motivated strategy of restricting some technologies and scaling up others to maintain social control.
